days.title: Northern Coast and Highlands
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Malin Head
stops.detail: At the tip of Inishowen is Malin Head, the northernmost point of Ireland.

stops.name: Slieve Snaght
stops.detail: The interior consists largely of hill ranges with the highest elevation, Slieve Snaght, at just over 600 m.

stops.name: Carrickabraghey
stops.detail: Well-known castle ruins include Carrickabraghey on the Isle of Doagh, the Norman castle in Greencastle, Inch Castle, Buncrana Castle and Elagh Castle.

days.title: Eastern Ports and Historic Forts
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Greencastle
stops.detail: Commercial fishing is still carried out from some port towns, e.g. from Greencastle, Bunagee and Leenan.

stops.name: Grianán von Aileach
stops.detail: Inishowen is home to many historical monuments dating back to the earliest settlement, such as the famous ring fort Grianán of Aileach and the ruins of several castles.

stops.name: Dunree Fort
stops.detail: Dunree Fort (today a military museum) and Neds Point Fort in the west of the peninsula

stops.name: Buncrana
stops.detail: Another connects Buncrana via Lough Swilly with Rathmullan on the Fanad peninsula in the west.

stops.name: Fahan
stops.detail: In the village of Fahan there is a small marina.

stops.name: Inch Island
stops.detail: Strictly speaking, Inch Island is no longer an island because, south of Fahan, it has a connection to the land via a dam.
